Maya Gebala, a 13-year-old survivor of the Feb. 10 shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School in British Columbia, has left BC Children’s Hospital after 262 days of treatment for severe brain injuries. The attack killed eight people, including six children, before the shooter, Jesse Van Rootselaar, died by suicide. Her father, David Gebala, announced her discharge on social media on Oct. 29, sharing a video in which Maya punched the air when he told her she was going home. He said doctors initially feared she would not survive the night and described her discharge as a milestone, while noting that her recovery will continue.

items.title: [npr.org] Alaska Native villages remain displaced a year after Typhoon Halong
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

A year after the remnants of Typhoon Halong destroyed homes and infrastructure in western Alaska, residents of Kipnuk and Kwigillingok remain displaced as repairs continue, with many unsure when they can return. The October 2025 storm affected more than 40 communities, and about 1,500 people were evacuated from Kwigillingok, Kipnuk and Nightmute. Alaska officials estimate that federal aid will make most Kipnuk homes livable by Thanksgiving, but say some residents need replacement housing. The state is seeking more funding. Both Kipnuk and Kwigillingok voted to relocate to higher ground, but current disaster funding is not designed to pay for moving the communities.

items.content_html:

Farmers in several countries face drought, flooding, rising input costs and weak returns. In Hungary, drought has cut agricultural output and prompted some growers to abandon corn; the central bank estimated that the damage reduced economic growth by 0.4 percentage points in 2026. Swedish farmers also face higher fertilizer and fuel costs ahead of spring planting, while a Spanish farm group says cereal producers are calculating whether crops can cover basic costs. Flooding in Colombia’s La Mojana region damaged crops and livestock, while a Polish pig farmer said low sale prices and extensive paperwork threatened farm viability. Proposals include improving water retention, adapting crops and linking farm credit to technical support. In Colombia, José Félix Lafaurie Rivera, president of the Colombian Cattle Ranchers Federation, urged the government to include measurable targets for farm advisory services and financing in its 2026-30 development plan.

items.title: [bbc.co.uk] Finland and Norway call Putin as Europe splits over Ukraine talks
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a 90-minute call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 27, pressing Ukraine’s position ahead of planned Russia-Ukraine-U.S. talks in Abu Dhabi in early November. The leaders said they initiated the call in consultation with Kyiv; Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said they urged concrete steps to de-escalate attacks on Ukraine’s energy facilities and infrastructure. Neither side announced a shift in position. The Kremlin said Putin argued that a lasting settlement required Russia’s interests to be taken fully and unconditionally into account and blamed European Union and NATO policies for prolonging the war; Støre said the conversation exposed “big differences”. The leaders agreed to keep speaking directly by phone, while making clear they spoke for their own countries, not Europe as a whole. The call drew a public rebuke from Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen, who said it was not coordinated with other Nordic leaders; Sweden’s Ulf Kristersson warned that separate initiatives could divide Europe’s voice. Ukraine backed the contact. The next trilateral meeting is expected after Nov. 4 in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: [cw39.com] Researchers favor permanent standard time as US debates clock changes
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Most U.S. clocks turn back one hour Nov. 1, as new research reviews renew debate over whether year-round standard time or daylight saving time better supports health. A Canadian policy analysis and a review focused on people with mental illness argue that permanent standard time better protects sleep, mood and biological rhythms. A broader review of population studies, however, finds a mix of harms and benefits from seasonal clock changes and summer daylight saving time. Permanent daylight saving time would delay winter sunrise, while permanent standard time would bring earlier summer sunrises and winter sunsets. The U.S. House passed a bill to make daylight saving time permanent in July 2026, but the Senate has not taken it up. The next seasonal clock change is scheduled for March 14, 2027.

The companies also differ over whether regulators should be able to suspend deployment or rely on company-run safeguards. President Trump has favored voluntary, “morally binding” industry controls and argued that stricter rules could weaken U.S. competition with China. Polling in Ohio and Iowa found strong support for a range of safety measures, and local opposition to data centers has led to ballot measures in dozens of U.S. jurisdictions. The White House says it seeks both American leadership and consumer protection.

items.title: [firstpost.com] Brazil markets slide as Lula win revives fiscal concerns
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Brazil-linked assets fell in early offshore trading Monday after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Investors had favored Bolsonaro, whom they viewed as more likely to pursue fiscal austerity and deregulation. An exchange-traded fund tracking Brazilian equities fell as much as 16% in Japan, while the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF dropped nearly 20% in overnight trading; currency derivatives signaled a possible decline of more than 10% in the real. These were early offshore moves, not Brazilian closing prices. Brazil’s electoral court gave Lula 51.79% of the vote to Bolsonaro’s 48.21%. Lula’s next term begins in January 2027. Public debt reached 82.9% of GDP in August, up more than 10 percentage points during Lula’s current term, while less than 8% of the federal budget is adjustable. Lula has pledged to protect social spending and raise the minimum wage. Investors are watching whether he can meet those pledges while stabilizing debt and inflation. Brazil’s benchmark interest rate was 13.75% and inflation was 4.6%. Inflation is not expected to reach the central bank’s 3% target until as late as 2029, Reuters reported. A consumption-tax overhaul approved in 2023 is also due to take effect in January, but the government has not disclosed its effective rate; independent analysts estimate it at about 28%.

items.title: [abcnews.com] Swift telescope shutdown ends rapid alerts for cosmic explosions
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

NASA shut down its Swift Observatory in late October after it could no longer hold steady enough for observations, ending a 22-year mission to detect gamma-ray bursts, supernovas and other high-energy events. Swift’s rapid observations helped direct other space telescopes toward eruptions for more detailed study, and astronomers are working out how to replace that alert function. The observatory resumed observations after the rescue effort ended and captured additional gamma-ray bursts and other ultrahigh-energy events before NASA turned off its systems. Over its mission, Swift recorded more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 exploding stars.
